subject: Stellix commercial terms: pricing tiers, minimum commit & tax handling
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@stellix.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stellix commercial questions on the draft order

Hi Ben / Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. We ran this past procurement and finance and have a handful of commercial items we'd like to clarify before we move to signatures:

- Pricing tiers: the schedule in Appendix A jumps from 500k to 1.5M with a steep step. Is there room for an intermediate slab for Q3 that better matches our expected usage?
- Minimum commit: can we phase the commit (25% / 35% / 40%) over three invoices instead of a single upfront?
- Net terms: our standard is Net45 for new vendors. Can Redwood accept Net45 for the first 12 months?
- Invoicing entity & taxes: we need clarity on whether Redwood will issue invoices to our US entity (Stellix Health Inc.) or our EU subsidiary. Also, who is responsible for VAT/withholding?
- Price adjustment clause: procurement is concerned about the auto-escalation language in §3.4. We prefer fixed pricing for the first contract year.

I've attached the version we annotated (attachment: stellix_orderform_v1.pdf) with inline comments.

Can we set a short call tomorrow to walk through? Jason Hill (procurement) will join from our side.

Best,
Olivia

Subject: Re: Stellix commercial questions on the draft order

Ben / Markus — I've pulled finance and legal input and sketched a commercial counter that I think addresses Stellix's asks while preserving Redwood's risks. High level notes: 

1) Pricing slabs: propose inserting a mid-slab at 750k with prorated unit price between the 500k and 1.5M brackets. This reduces cliff risk for both sides.
2) Minimum commit phasing: accept phased commit (25/35/40) but require first tranche invoiced upfront as non-refundable activation fee; subsequent tranches invoiced quarterly against usage with reconciliation at month 10.
3) Net terms: we can accept Net45 for the first 12 months but need Net30 thereafter unless they provide a credit approval letter. This is conditional on credit review.
4) Tax & invoicing: prefer to invoice Stellix Health Inc. (US entity) by default. If they request EU invoicing, we'll need a tax residency certificate and to re-route billing to the appropriate Redwood entity. Redwood will not gross-up for customer withholding; instead the contract will allow for deduction of required withholding with evidence and a tax indemnity language.
5) Price adjustment clause: we can cap any annual price adjustment to 3% and require 60 days' notice. If customer insists on fixed pricing, reduce to 0% for year 1 only.

I attached the redline doc with inline suggested language (attachment: KP_orderform_redlines.docx) and a short CSV that models invoice timing and cash flow for the proposed phasing (attachment: commercial_summary.csv).

Edits to legal: @Karthik — see §2.1 (min commit), §3.4 (price adj), §7.2 (tax withholding). Please advise on any mandatory toggles.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

Date: 2025-08-06T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stellix commercial questions on the draft order

Olivia — thanks for the annotated PDF and the list.

Quick summary from our side based on Kim's review:
- We're open to a middle pricing slab (proposal: 750k) to smooth the step.
- Phased minimum commit is ok; Redwood requires the first tranche as an activation (non-refundable) invoice. The remainder can be invoiced quarterly with a reconciliation run.
- We can agree Net45 for the first 12 months, after which Net30 applies unless you provide standard credit references.
- For taxes: default billing to Stellix Health Inc. (US). If Stellix requires EU invoicing then we'll need the appropriate tax residency docs and we'll add a clause that allows for deduction for withholding taxes with evidence and an indemnity.
- Price changes: we can cap annual increases to 3% and offer a 0% cap for year one if that's required to get to signature.

Two quick asks for you before we bring this to legal redline: 1) confirm which entity should receive invoices (US or EU), and 2) confirm Jason's availability for the 8/6 call at 2:00pm PT.

I've attached a one-page commercial summary for ease (attachment: commercial_summary.csv).

If those two items are confirmed we'll route an updated order form to DocuSign plus a limited set of legal edits to Karthik.

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
